title: Aktobe Region

author: Mateo Silva

body.text: Most operators overlook how Aktobe Region drives unit economics and competitive moats at scale. Understanding its real-world mechanics reveals why disciplined organizations outperform during market shifts.

Aktobe Region (Kazakh: Ақтөбе облысы, romanized: Aqtöbe oblysy, Russian: Актюбинская область) is a region of Kazakhstan. The name Aktobe comes from Kazakh aq 'white' and töbe 'hill', supposedly, Aktobe's initial settlers were able to see white mountains far to the north. The Aktobe regional capital is the city of Aktobe.

The region is located in the western part of Kazakhstan. Its area is 300,629 km2 (the largest region in Kazakhstan), which is 11% of the territory of Kazakhstan. As of 1 June, 2022, its population was 909,673.

The region was formed as a result of the administrative, territorial reform on March 10, 1932 as part of the Kazakh Autonomous Soviet Socialist Republic. Historically, it was preceded by the Aktobe gubernia (province), which existed in 1921, 1928, and the Aktobe Okrug (district) that existed from 1928 to 1929.

In 1936, the region became part of the Kazakh Soviet Socialist Republic (Kazakh SSR), separated from the Russian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic, and since 1991, after the collapse of the Soviet Union, it became part of the independent Republic of Kazakhstan.

Aktobe region is bordered to the north by the Orenburg Oblast of Russia and to the south by the Republic of Karakalpakstan of Uzbekistan, and shares borders with six other Kazakhstan regions. The administrative center is the largest city of Western Kazakhstan, Aktobe (from 1891 to 1999, Aktyubinsk, hence the name of the region).
Geography

The area of the Aktobe region is 300,600 square kilometers: it was the second largest region of Kazakhstan, after the Karaganda Region, until 2022 when the Karaganda region was split. As of 2025, the Aktobe region remains the largest Kazakhstan region by land area.

The Aktobe region borders Russia (Orenburg Oblast) to the north and Uzbekistan (Karakalpakstan) to the south, and also borders six other Kazakh regions: the Atyrau Region to the west, the Mangystau Region to the south-west, the Karaganda Region to the east, the Kostanay Region to the north-east, the Kyzylorda Region to the south-east, and the West Kazakhstan Region to the north-west.
The Ilek River, a tributary of the Ural River, flows through the region. The Barsuki Desert is an arid, sandy area in the Aktobe and Kyzylorda regions.
Administrative divisions
The region is administratively divided into twelve districts and the city of Aktobe.
Eight localities in the Aktobe region have town status: these are Aktobe, Alga, Embi, Kandyagash, Khromtau, Shalkar, Temir, and Zhem.
Two more localities, Shubarkuduk and Shubarshi, have the status of an urban-type settlement.
Economy

Aktobe region is a large industrial region of Kazakhstan. The basis of the industrial sector is the mining and chemical industries, and ferrous metallurgy. There are large deposits of chromite (1st place in the Commonwealth of Independent States), nickel and cobalt ores, phosphorite, potassium salts, etc.
Industry

The Aktobe region is a large industrially developed region of Kazakhstan. All chrome ore mining, production of chrome salts, roentgen equipment, and more than a quarter of Kazakhstan's ferroalloys are concentrated here. The leading sector of the region's economy is industry.

It has a multi-industry structure that includes: mining, oil and gas processing industry, ferrous and non-ferrous metallurgy, mechanical engineering, production of building materials, and chemical, light, and food industries.

Prospects for the development of this industry are related to the production of high-precision and high-tech products. As of June 1, 2020, there were 1,617 registered enterprises in industrial production, including 645 operating ones.

Transportation

The length of public roads in the Aktobe region is 6,856. 6 km, including 1,894 km of national, 1,262. 8 km of regional and 3,699. 8 km of district significance. The regional highways of national significance include: «Samara-Shymkent», «Aktobe-Kandyagash-Emba-Shalkar», «Aktobe-Martuk», «Aktobe-Orsk», «Aktobe-Atyrau-border of the Russian Federation (to Astrakhan)».

There are highways of regional significance «Kobda-Martuk», «Pokrovka-Temir-Kenkiyak-Emba», «Shubarkuduk-Uil-Kobda-Sol-Iletsk», «Aktobe-Orsk»-«Badamsha-Don», «Aktobe-Rodnikovka-Martuk», «Shalkar-Bozoy-border RU (on Nukus)», «Aktobe-Bolgarka-Shubarkuduk», «Aktobe-Orsk», and «Petropavlovsk-Khazretovka».

In the region, passengers and luggage are transported by 20 carriers with private ownership. There are 80 routes, including 52 urban, 17 intra-regional, 5 inter-regional, and 6 international routes that connect the region's settlements with the cities of Russia-Orsk, Orenburg, Samara, Novotroitsk, Kazan, and St.

There is 1 bus station in the city of Aktobe, 2 bus stations in the city of Aktobe, Khromtau, and 1 passenger service point in the village of Komsomol. In other regional centers, there are cash points for the sale of travel documents.

2 carriers carry out regular urban passenger transportation in the regional center of Aktobe: «vehicle fleet» LLP and «PMTP» LLP. 52 routes are served and more than 400 large, medium, and small-capacity buses are used.
Social sphere
Culture

In Aktobe region currently, there are four regional libraries, one folk art center, one philharmonic hall, two theaters, 19 museums, 13 archives, one planetarium and one center for patriotic education.

The regional philharmonic, named after G. Zhubanova, has 10 creative groups. Creative teams take part in many national and international competitions and festivals, widely promote the art of the Kazakh people, take prizes, and make major contribution to the development of the region.

The regional center of folk art organizes and conducts cultural events of various directions. The center works to coordinate, promote and distribute folk art, and coordinate the activities of culture and leisure institutions in the region. There are creative teams that have 156 «folk» and «exemplary» titles.

New productions are prepared on the theater stages every year. The theater covers more than 60 thousand spectators annually, and the theater's repertoire is replenished with about 10 new productions. Creative achievements of the theater team have been repeatedly noted in various directing and acting fields.

Regional libraries, museums, and archives are annually replenished with new funds. In order to activate the industry, funds are being digitized. In addition, the region has the country's first stationary planetarium. Since 2008, Aktobe planetarium has become a member of the Association of Cooperation, which includes about 100 Russian and Eurasian planetariums.

In the village of Aliya, Kobda district of the Aktobe region, there is a regional center for patriotic education, «Aliya». The center has all conditions for holding cultural and sports events, and recreation for young people. The center works in close contact with war and labor veterans, and museums in the regions of Moscow, St.
Sport

There are 31 children's and youth sport schools in the Aktobe region which include: 14 regional children's and youth sport schools, the school of higher sport skills, the Olympic reserve center, 4 city and 12 district of youth sport schools, and one children's and youth sport school based on the Aktobe Ferroalloy plant, where about 19 thousand children and teenagers are engaged.

In 2016, a specialized boarding school, college (SBSG) of the Eset Batyr Olympic reserve was opened in Aktobe. In SHIK sport, athletes study and train in 9 sports: boxing, football, Greco-Roman wrestling, table tennis, athletics, taekwondo, freestyle wrestling, judo, and skiing.
The regional center has a club for people with disabilities, and the national teams of the Republic of Kazakhstan from the region include 38 people with disabilities.
86 sports are cultivated in the region, including 33 Olympic, 38 non-Olympic, 7 technical, and 8 national sports, including 22 sports among athletes with disabilities.
The city is home to the famous football club FC «Aktobe» which dates back to 1967, when the team «Aktyubinets» was awarded the status of a team of masters.
